raw.title: Head of Equity Administration
raw.description:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly experienced Head of Equity Administration to own and scale our global equity administration function as we prepare for the next stage of growth and potential public-company readiness.

This leader will be responsible for the end-to-end administration, governance, controls, reporting, and employee experience associated with our equity programs. The role will partner closely with Legal, Finance, Accounting, Tax, People, Payroll, Compensation, and senior leadership, and will play a critical role in building the infrastructure, processes, and controls required for a complex late-stage private company and future public company.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in equity compensation with strong operational judgment, systems experience, attention to detail, and the ability to lead through significant organizational change.

Key Responsibilities

Equity Plan Administration

  • Own the day-to-day and strategic administration of the company’s equity compensation programs, including stock options, RSUs, restricted stock, and other equity-based awards.

  • Manage the complete equity lifecycle, including grants, vesting, exercises, releases, cancellations, terminations, repurchases, transfers, and settlement.

  • Maintain accurate equity records, capitalization data, participant information, and supporting documentation.

  • Oversee equity administration platforms, workflows, integrations, and vendor relationships.

  • Establish scalable policies, procedures, controls, and service-level standards for equity administration.

IPO and Public Company Readiness

  • Serve as a key functional leader in IPO-readiness efforts related to equity compensation and capitalization.

  • Assess current processes and implement the systems, controls, governance, and documentation required to operate effectively as a public company.

  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Accounting, Payroll, Tax, Compensation, Internal Audit, external counsel, auditors, and other advisors on IPO preparation and ongoing compliance.

  • Support preparation for public-company equity administration requirements, including Section 16 processes, insider-related workflows, trading-window administration, Rule 10b5-1 plans, and related controls, as applicable.

  • Develop processes to support future employee stock purchase plans and other public-company equity programs, where relevant.

Compliance, Accounting, Tax, and Controls

  • Ensure equity administration processes comply with applicable securities, tax, accounting, and corporate governance requirements.

  • Partner with Accounting on stock-based compensation reporting, reconciliations, audit support, and financial close processes.

  • Partner with Tax and Payroll on equity-related tax withholding, reporting, settlement, mobility, and international compliance.

  • Support compliance with applicable requirements including ASC 718, Section 409A, securities regulations, and relevant international equity rules.

  • Design and maintain strong internal controls, including controls supporting future SOX compliance.

  • Lead regular reconciliations among the equity administration platform, general ledger, payroll systems, HR systems, and capitalization records.

Global Equity Operations

  • Oversee equity administration across multiple jurisdictions and ensure local operational requirements are appropriately supported.

  • Partner with Legal, Tax, and external advisors to address country-specific securities, tax, payroll, exchange-control, and reporting obligations.

  • Establish scalable processes for internationally mobile employees and cross-border equity issues.

  • Maintain global equity compliance calendars and operational documentation.

Governance and Board Support

  • Partner with Legal and executive leadership on equity governance, board and compensation committee approvals, grant processes, and plan administration.

  • Maintain accurate records of board-approved equity activity and ensure timely execution of approved grants.

  • Support preparation of equity-related materials for the Board and Compensation Committee.

  • Monitor share utilization, equity plan reserves, dilution, burn rate, and other relevant equity metrics in partnership with Finance and Compensation.

Employee Experience

  • Serve as a trusted resource for employees and executives regarding equity compensation.

  • Develop clear, scalable communications and educational materials to help employees understand their equity.

  • Establish efficient processes for employee inquiries, transactions, and issue resolution.

  • Partner with People and Compensation teams on equity communications associated with hiring, promotions, refresh grants, liquidity events, and other programs.

Team and Function Leadership

  • Build and lead a high-performing equity administration function capable of supporting the company through IPO and beyond.

  • Develop operating metrics, service standards, control frameworks, and reporting for the function.

  • Evaluate team structure, technology, vendor relationships, and outsourcing opportunities as the company scales.

  • Act as the company’s subject-matter expert on equity administration and contribute to broader compensation and corporate-governance initiatives.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in stock administration, equity compensation, legal operations, compensation, finance, or a related field, with substantial direct ownership of equity administration.

  • Significant experience supporting a late-stage private company, public company, IPO process, or major capital-markets transaction.

  • Deep knowledge of equity compensation vehicles and administration, including stock options and RSUs.

  • Strong understanding of equity-related securities, tax, payroll, accounting, and governance considerations.

  • Experience with ASC 718 and equity-related financial reporting and controls.

  • Familiarity with public-company requirements such as Section 16, Rule 10b5-1 plans, insider trading controls, and SOX environments.

  • Experience administering equity programs for a global employee population strongly preferred.

  • Demonstrated experience with equity administration platforms such as Morgan Stanley at Work/Shareworks or Fidelity, Carta, E*TRADE, Computershare, or similar systems.

  • Strong analytical skills and ability to manage complex datasets and reconciliations.

  • Exceptional attention to detail, judgment, organization, and discretion.

  • Strong executive communication skills and the ability to partner effectively across Legal, Finance, Accounting, Tax, Payroll, HR, and Compensation.

  • Proven ability to build processes and controls in a rapidly scaling environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CEP designation or similar equity compensation credential.

  • Experience leading equity administration through an IPO.

  • Experience implementing or migrating equity administration platforms.

  • Experience establishing SOX-compliant equity processes and controls.

  • Experience launching an ESPP or other public-company equity programs.

  • Experience managing equity programs across multiple international jurisdictions.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 12–18 months, the Head of Equity Administration will have:

  • Established a highly accurate, scalable, and well-controlled equity administration function.

  • Built clear ownership, documentation, and operating procedures across the equity lifecycle.

  • Strengthened reconciliations, controls, audit readiness, and cross-functional governance.

  • Prepared the equity function for public-company operating requirements.

  • Improved the employee and executive experience around equity compensation.

  • Created the organizational, systems, and process foundation required to support the company through IPO and continued growth.

Reporting Relationship

This role may report to the General Counsel, Head of People, Total Rewards, Head of Finance, or another senior executive, depending on the company’s organizational structure.

The Head of Equity Administration will work closely with senior leaders across Legal, Finance, Accounting, Tax, People, Payroll, Compensation, and Investor Relations.

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

What You’ll Do

  • Own Fireworks AI’s global revenue accounting function, including revenue recognition, contract review, close, reconciliations, reporting, and related controls.

  • Serve as the company’s technical accounting expert for revenue recognition under ASC 606.

  • Review complex and non-standard customer contracts and determine the appropriate accounting treatment.

  • Prepare and maintain technical accounting memos supporting revenue recognition conclusions and significant judgments.

  • Partner closely with Sales, Legal, Deal Desk, FP&A, Billing, and Finance to evaluate the accounting implications of new products, pricing models, and contract structures.

  • Establish scalable revenue accounting policies, processes, and controls as the company grows.

  • Lead monthly and quarterly revenue close activities, including deferred revenue, contract assets and liabilities, variable consideration, and revenue-related balance sheet accounts.

  • Support external audits and serve as the primary point of contact for revenue-related accounting matters.

  • Identify opportunities to automate and improve revenue accounting workflows, systems, and data integrity.

  • Build and lead a high-performing revenue accounting team over time.

  • Support broader technical accounting initiatives, financial reporting requirements, and readiness for future public-company standards.

What We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, with substantial experience in technical revenue accounting.

  • Deep expertise in ASC 606 and experience applying the standard to complex technology or SaaS contracts.

  • Strong understanding of usage-based, consumption-based, subscription, and enterprise contract structures.

  • Experience evaluating non-standard terms such as minimum commitments, prepaid credits, discounts, rebates, service-level arrangements, contract modifications, and variable consideration.

  • Strong technical accounting research and memo-writing skills.

  • Experience working in a high-growth technology company; experience with AI, cloud infrastructure, developer platforms, SaaS, or consumption-based businesses is especially relevant.

  • Prior experience managing revenue close processes, internal controls, and external audit relationships.

  • Ability to partner effectively with commercial teams while maintaining sound accounting judgment and appropriate controls.

  • Strong systems orientation and experience scaling revenue accounting processes through automation.

  • CPA strongly preferred.

  • Public accounting experience, particularly with a Big Four firm, is preferred.

What Success Looks Like

You will build a technically rigorous and scalable revenue accounting function that enables Fireworks AI to grow quickly while maintaining accurate financial reporting. You will be a trusted advisor on complex deals and new business models, ensuring that revenue accounting considerations are understood early and reflected appropriately in the company’s financial statements.

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

raw.description:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced and commercially minded Head of Procurement to lead our procurement function and shape the company’s sourcing, supplier management, and purchasing strategy.

This role will be responsible for building a high-performing procurement organization that delivers measurable cost efficiencies, improves supplier performance, strengthens commercial discipline, and reduces supply and operational risk. The Head of Procurement will partner closely with business leaders across Finance, Operations, Legal, Technology, and other functions to ensure procurement supports both near-term business needs and long-term company objectives.

The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with strong execution, commercial negotiation expertise, stakeholder management skills, and the ability to build scalable procurement processes in a growing organization.

Key Responsibilities

Procurement Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and execute the company-wide procurement strategy aligned with business and financial objectives.

  • Establish procurement policies, operating models, governance, and approval frameworks.

  • Build procurement into a strategic business partner rather than a transactional purchasing function.

  • Identify and prioritize opportunities for cost optimization, supplier consolidation, process improvement, and risk reduction.

  • Provide leadership and coaching to the procurement team and build organizational capability as the function grows.

Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management

  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across key spend categories.

  • Develop category strategies based on spend analysis, market intelligence, supplier capabilities, and business requirements.

  • Lead or support high-value and complex commercial negotiations.

  • Drive competitive sourcing processes including RFPs, RFQs, supplier evaluations, and contract negotiations.

  • Establish commercial benchmarks and ensure the organization receives competitive pricing, terms, and service levels.

  • Partner with Legal and Finance to improve contract structures, payment terms, renewal management, and commercial protections.

Supplier Management

  • Develop a structured supplier relationship management program for strategic and critical suppliers.

  • Establish supplier performance metrics, scorecards, business reviews, and improvement plans.

  • Identify supplier concentration, continuity, compliance, financial, geopolitical, and operational risks.

  • Develop mitigation strategies and alternative sourcing options for critical suppliers.

  • Build strategic relationships with key suppliers to support innovation, service improvement, and long-term value creation.

Spend Management & Value Creation

  • Create visibility into company-wide third-party spend and identify opportunities to improve purchasing effectiveness.

  • Establish savings methodologies and reporting in partnership with Finance.

  • Deliver measurable cost savings, cost avoidance, working capital improvements, and total cost-of-ownership benefits.

  • Improve demand management and challenge unnecessary or inefficient expenditure where appropriate.

  • Track procurement performance against agreed KPIs and communicate results to senior leadership.

Procurement Operations & Process

  • Design scalable procure-to-pay and source-to-contract processes.

  • Improve requisition, approval, purchase order, contracting, supplier onboarding, and invoice workflows.

  • Increase procurement adoption while creating an efficient experience for internal stakeholders.

  • Evaluate and implement procurement technologies, sourcing platforms, contract management systems, and analytics tools where appropriate.

  • Ensure procurement processes support appropriate financial controls, audit requirements, and regulatory obligations.

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Partner with senior executives and functional leaders to understand business priorities and upcoming purchasing requirements.

  • Advise stakeholders on sourcing strategies, supplier selection, commercial structures, and negotiation approaches.

  • Balance cost, speed, quality, innovation, service, and risk when making procurement recommendations.

  • Build strong relationships across the organization and influence decisions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Qualifications

  • Significant experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, category management, supply chain, or related commercial roles.

  • Demonstrated experience leading a procurement function or major procurement programs.

  • Strong record of delivering measurable commercial value through sourcing, negotiation, supplier management, and process improvement.

  • Experience negotiating complex, high-value supplier agreements.

  • Strong understanding of procurement governance, contracting, supplier risk, and spend management.

  • Experience managing and developing teams.

  • Strong financial and analytical capabilities, including the ability to evaluate business cases, pricing models, and total cost of ownership.

  • Excellent stakeholder management, influencing, communication, and negotiation skills.

  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment with competing priorities and incomplete information.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building or transforming a procurement function.

  • Experience operating in a high-growth or rapidly changing organization.

  • Familiarity with procurement technology, spend analytics, contract lifecycle management, and procure-to-pay platforms.

  • Experience managing both direct and indirect spend categories.

  • Professional procurement qualification such as CIPS, CPSM, or equivalent is advantageous.

Success Measures

Success in this role will be measured through outcomes such as:

  • Procurement savings and cost avoidance.

  • Percentage of addressable spend managed through procurement.

  • Supplier performance and risk reduction.

  • Improved commercial and contractual terms.

  • Procurement cycle times and stakeholder satisfaction.

  • Compliance with procurement policies and processes.

  • Increased spend visibility and forecasting accuracy.

  • Development of a strong, scalable procurement organization.

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

raw.title: Compute Financial Analyst
raw.description:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

About the Role

We are looking for a highly motivated and detail-oriented Financial Compute Analyst to join our Accounting team. This role will help build and run the accounting, allocation, and reporting for compute cost of revenue as the company continues to scale.

Compute is by far our largest expense category and the single biggest driver of gross margin. Cloud spend runs across a growing set of CSP and neocloud vendors under a mix of on-demand, reserved, prepaid, and committed-capacity structures — each with its own invoicing cadence, true-up mechanics, and credit terms. The ideal candidate is comfortable turning GPU utilization data into defensible accounting conclusions and enjoys building the schedules, reconciliations, and controls that make cost of revenue accurate, explainable, and auditable.

This is a hands-on role that will partner closely with Infrastructure, Capital Efficiency, FP&A, Procurement, Partnerships, and Data teams to ensure compute costs are captured in the right period, classified to the right cost center, and reported in a way the business can actually use.

Responsibilities

  • Support the monthly close for compute cost of revenue, including preparing cloud cost journal entries, accruals for unbilled usage, prepaid amortization, true-ups to actual usage, and supporting schedules.

  • Perform reconciliations of GPU utilization data to CSP invoices, contracted capacity, and the general ledger; research utilization-to-billed variances, idle capacity, and billing discrepancies, and escalate complex items with a proposed resolution.

  • Prepare and maintain prepaid cloud balance schedules, including short-term/long-term classification, amortization tied to committed capacity, and rollforwards that tie to contract terms, for senior review.

  • Support the accounting for complex vendor and partnership arrangements, including committed spend, prepayment and reimbursement structures, revenue share, SLA and downtime credits, and capacity arranged through third parties.

  • Help evaluate the accounting treatment of new vendor agreements and capacity commitments, including COGS vs. operating expense classification, gross vs. net presentation, embedded leases under ASC 842, and liability vs. expense characterization.

  • Work with Data and Analytics teams to build and validate the cost and utilization data pipelines that feed allocations and reporting, and improve data quality at the source.

  • Contribute to technical accounting memos supporting significant cost of revenue and capitalization conclusions, including capitalized software and its amortization into COGS.

  • Support external audits by preparing cost schedules, vendor contract samples, allocation support, and responses to auditor inquiries.

  • Identify opportunities to automate and scale cost accounting processes, reconciliations, and reporting as compute spend grows.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

  • CPA or CPA candidate a plus.

  • 3–6 years of relevant accounting or finance experience, including meaningful experience in cost accounting or cost of revenue.

  • Familiarity with cost allocation concepts, including direct cost attribution and overhead allocation across cost centers or product lines.

  • Experience in cloud computing, AI infrastructure, SaaS, or other usage/consumption-based business models is preferred but not required.

  • Experience evaluating vendor contracts and committed purchase arrangements, and translating commercial terms into accounting treatment, is a plus.

raw.title: Strategic Finance & Operations Manager
raw.description:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

The Role

As Strategic Finance & Operations Lead, you'll sit at the intersection of revenue, go-to-market, and financial strategy — owning the financial models, pricing frameworks, and operational processes that power Fireworks' commercial engine. This is a high-visibility, high-ownership role that works directly with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Engineering leaders to drive deals forward and help the business scale intelligently.

If you love turning ambiguity into structured frameworks and enjoy being the finance partner who actually accelerates revenue (not just reports on it) — this is your role.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build dynamic financial and operating models to evaluate new sales strategies and pricing models, accelerating topline growth while balancing competitiveness with margin health

  • Work closely with sales team on customer contracts, with cross collaboration with engineering, product, and finance to operationalize and recognize new product offers

  • Identify and drive opportunities for process automation, bringing structure with a continuous lens of improvement to reduce friction and cycle time

  • Support Sales leaders with funnel analysis and pipeline visibility for sales-led accounts, turning CRM data into actionable financial insight

  • Support revenue and demand forecasting, necessary for resource allocation and planning for cross-functional stakeholders across GTM, Engineering, and Product

  • Assist with capital planning efforts, corporate finance, or investor relations, as needed

Who You Are

  • A structured thinker who moves fast. You can build a rigorous model from scratch and ship it before the week is over.

  • A cross-functional operator. You're equally comfortable in a product roadmap discussion, a sales deal review, and a finance close meeting — and you know how to earn trust across each.

  • A business partner, not a scorekeeper. You don't just report what happened; you help shape what happens next.

  • Detail-obsessed but never lost in the weeds. You hold yourself to a high standard of accuracy and can also zoom out to tell the story behind the numbers.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. Fireworks is scaling fast. You'll build processes and frameworks where none currently exist.

Qualifications

Required

  • 4+ years of experience in strategic finance, investment banking, or management consulting

  • Demonstrated experience building financial models from scratch

  • Strong proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets; experience working with CRM data (Salesforce or equivalent)

  • Excellent communication skills — able to translate financial analysis into clear recommendations for non-finance audiences

  • Experience or strong interest in using AI agents and tooling to develop efficient workstreams that deliver high-quality results

Preferred

  • Experience at a high-growth SaaS or infrastructure company; prior exposure to usage-based pricing models is a strong plus

  • Familiarity with revenue recognition principles and billing systems

  • Experience designing or administering sales compensation plans

  • Comfort working with highly technical data and familiarity with SQL / BigQuery to pull and analyze data independently

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

raw.title: Office Manager, New York
raw.description:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

As Office Manager, you run our New York office and make it a place people want to come to. The office is open, but the operational foundation is still to be built: few local vendors, no established rhythm, and a team growing fast. You run the office day to day as it grows from a handful of people to a full regional site, and you help put the foundation underneath it.

Day to day, you are the person who makes the office work: the space, the vendors, the onboarding, the events, the visitors, and the hundred small things that decide whether a team is set up to do its best work. You also set the atmosphere. A lot of what makes an office somewhere people choose to be comes down to who runs it.

This is an in-office role in New York, and you will be at the office five days of the week. It suits a hands-on operator who likes being first in: equally comfortable pushing a vendor contract over the line and sorting the catering order, and proud of a team that never has to think about logistics.

We care more about how good you are than how many years you have done this. If you are early in your career but have a clear record of excelling at whatever you took on, we want to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities

  • Office: Run our New York office end to end: the relationship with the landlord or workspace provider, access and security, health and safety, the cleaning and facilities vendors, supplies, and the day-to-day running of the space.

  • Atmosphere and Team Rhythm: Own the office cadence, from lunches and all-hands setup to team dinners and offsites. For customer and community events, partner with our Field Marketing team, who own the programmes, ensuring everything hosted at the office runs smoothly.

  • Onboarding: Make every new joiner productive on day one: equipment, access, desk, local paperwork, and a proper welcome. Handle offboarding just as cleanly.

  • Visitors: Host visiting executives, customers, and candidates, and make sure their time at the office runs smoothly.

  • Vendors and Budget: Select and manage local vendors (landlord or workspace provider, IT and device provisioning, AV, catering, cleaning, security, insurance) and own the office budget, invoices, and renewals.

Minimum Qualifications

A demonstrable record of excellence in whatever you have done so far (office management, operations, a startup, a fast-paced team, or elsewhere), where you were clearly one of the best at it. Years of experience matter less than this.

  • Fast learner with real curiosity: comfortable learning new skills that may be needed in the office with no clear owner, and knowing when to bring in expert help.

  • Hands-on with vendors and negotiation, or the confidence and judgment to become so quickly.

  • Highly organised, with a track record of running many parallel workstreams to completion without being chased.

  • Comfortable operating with autonomy in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment; you build the process rather than wait for it.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication and a service mindset toward the team.

  • Warm, calm under pressure, and the kind of person people go to first. This role sets the tone of the office.

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

raw.title: Head of Process & Controls - Finance and Operations
raw.description:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

We are seeking a Head of Process & Controls to build and lead the operational processes, controls, and governance required to scale our AI infrastructure business.

This role will own the end-to-end process architecture across AI infrastructure workflows, token and usage accuracy, Order-to-Cash (O2C), and Purchase-to-Pay (P2P), with a strong mandate to build the process foundation, remediate and simplify existing workflows, and drive AI-enabled automation.

The leader will take a phased transformation approach:

Build the foundation →Standardize → Automate and scale with AI.

The objective is to create reliable, well-controlled processes that accurately connect infrastructure consumption to customer billing, supplier costs, accounting, and financial reporting—while progressively reducing manual effort, reconciliation burden, operational discrepancies, and financial leakage.

The ideal candidate combines strong process transformation and controls expertise with an understanding of cloud and AI infrastructure economics. They will work across Engineering, Infrastructure, Product, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Sales Operations, and Data teams to create scalable workflows and embed automation into the operating model.

Key Responsibilities

Process Foundation, Standardization & Transformation

Build the foundational process architecture for AI infrastructure and related financial operations.

Define clear end-to-end processes, ownership, controls, decision rights, system-of-records, data handoffs, approval points, exception paths, and escalation procedures.

Assess the current operating environment and identify:

  • Fragmented or undocumented processes

  • Manual workarounds

  • Spreadsheet-dependent workflows

  • Duplicate activities

  • Unclear process ownership

  • Control gaps

  • Inconsistent data definitions

  • Reconciliation issues

  • System integration gaps

  • Recurring operational and financial discrepancies

Lead the Standardization of existing processes before introducing automation, ensuring that inefficient or poorly controlled processes are not simply automated in their current state.

Develop standard operating procedures, process maps, RACI frameworks, control matrices, data definitions, and operational playbooks.

Establish consistent process and control standards across functions, regions, products, customers, and infrastructure providers.

Create a transformation roadmap that prioritizes foundational process improvements, risk remediation, automation opportunities, and scalable system capabilities.

AI Automation & Manual Effort Reduction

Lead the transition from manual and reactive operations toward AI-enabled, automated process execution and controls.

Identify high-volume, repetitive, reconciliation-intensive, and exception-driven activities that can be automated.

Partner with Engineering, Data, Finance Systems, and Product teams to implement AI-enabled workflows for areas such as:

  • Automated usage reconciliation

  • Token and compute anomaly detection

  • Customer billing validation

  • Vendor invoice validation

  • Contract-to-billing checks

  • Purchase-order and invoice matching

  • Revenue and cost leakage identification

  • Accrual estimation

  • Data-quality monitoring

  • Exception classification and routing

  • Root-cause analysis

  • Variance investigation

  • Duplicate or missing transaction detection

  • Automated control evidence collection

  • Operational reporting and management insights

Design processes around exception-based management, where systems and AI handle routine transactions and teams focus primarily on material exceptions, judgment, and remediation.

Establish measurable targets for reducing manual touchpoints, spreadsheet dependency, reconciliation effort, processing time, error rates, and discrepancies.

Ensure AI-enabled automation includes appropriate governance, human review, traceability, validation, and controls.

Workflow & Process Governance

Standardize the end-to-end process framework for AI infrastructure operations, from infrastructure provisioning and consumption through usage measurement, customer billing, vendor settlement, accounting, and reporting.

Map and optimize workflows across compute, GPU, model inference, API and token consumption, capacity allocation, and related infrastructure services.

Establish clear process ownership, approval points, system interfaces, data handoffs, service-level expectations, exception management, and escalation procedures.

Partner with Engineering and Infrastructure teams to design operational processes that remain scalable as AI workloads, customers, infrastructure providers, and commercial models grow.

Ensure controls and financial requirements are embedded into infrastructure workflows by design rather than added downstream.

Token & Usage Accuracy

Standardize framework governing the accuracy, completeness, and traceability of AI token and infrastructure usage data.

Ensure reliable measurement and reconciliation of metrics such as:

  • Input and output tokens

  • API consumption

  • Model inference usage

  • GPU or accelerator utilization

  • Compute hours

  • Storage and network consumption

  • Reserved and on-demand capacity

  • Customer-specific infrastructure consumption

Establish automated reconciliations between infrastructure telemetry, metering platforms, pricing systems, customer contracts, billing systems, supplier data, and the general ledger.

Develop preventive and detective controls to identify:

  • Missing usage

  • Duplicate usage

  • Incorrect token counts

  • Incorrect pricing

  • Unbilled consumption

  • Misallocated consumption

  • Customer/vendor usage mismatches

  • Unexpected consumption patterns

  • Data pipeline failures

Partner with Data and Engineering teams to establish authoritative data sources, common definitions, and end-to-end data lineage from infrastructure activity through financial reporting.

Drive continuous improvement in token accuracy, usage completeness, billing accuracy, and cost attribution.

Order-to-Cash

Own and continuously improve the end-to-end Order-to-Cash process, including:

contract / order → provisioning → usage capture → rating and pricing → invoicing → accounts receivable → collections → revenue reporting.

Build a standardized and scalable O2C foundation that supports both committed and consumption-based business models.

Ensure customer contracts, pricing structures, committed capacity, minimum spend agreements, usage-based pricing, credits, and discounts are correctly translated into operational and billing systems.

Establish automated controls over usage-to-invoice reconciliation and billing completeness.

Reduce manual billing adjustments and recurring discrepancies through better upstream data quality, system integration, and automated validation.

Develop processes for billing adjustments, credits, disputes, contract amendments, and usage exceptions.

Partner with Revenue Accounting to ensure operational processes support accurate and timely revenue recognition.

Drive improvements in billing accuracy, invoice timeliness, collections, customer experience, and revenue leakage prevention.

Purchase-to-Pay

Own and optimize the Purchase-to-Pay process for AI infrastructure and related services, including:

capacity planning → purchase commitment → purchase order → service consumption → invoice validation → accrual → payment → supplier reconciliation.

Build a standardized P2P foundation connecting procurement commitments, infrastructure usage, supplier contracts, invoices, and accounting.

Establish controls ensuring vendor invoices accurately reflect contracted pricing and actual infrastructure consumption.

Reduce manual invoice review and reconciliation through AI-enabled invoice validation and exception detection.

Partner with Infrastructure and Procurement teams on commitments for cloud services, GPUs, data centers, networking, model providers, and other infrastructure vendors.

Develop processes for committed-use agreements, prepaid capacity, minimum commitments, volume discounts, credits, and variable consumption charges.

Ensure appropriate accruals and cost allocations where supplier invoices lag infrastructure consumption.

Financial & Operational Controls

Design and maintain a scalable controls framework across infrastructure operations and financial processes.

Define preventive and detective controls covering:

  • Usage completeness and accuracy

  • Token accuracy

  • Pricing accuracy

  • Customer billing

  • Supplier invoicing

  • Revenue completeness

  • Infrastructure cost completeness

  • Contract compliance

  • Approval authorities

  • Reconciliations

  • Data integrity

  • Manual adjustments

Prioritize automated controls over manual controls wherever technically and operationally feasible.

Establish control owners, evidence requirements, review frequencies, exception thresholds, and remediation processes.

Create automated exception monitoring so discrepancies can be identified close to the point of occurrence rather than through downstream month-end reconciliation.

Partner with Accounting, Internal Audit, and external auditors to support financial reporting and audit requirements.

Where applicable, build processes and controls capable of supporting SOX-compliant operations.

Process Automation, Systems & Data Architecture

Drive automation across infrastructure-to-finance workflows and systematically reduce reliance on spreadsheets, manual reconciliations, and human intervention.

Partner with Product, Engineering, Finance Systems, and Data teams to define requirements for:

  • Usage metering

  • Rating and pricing

  • Billing

  • Procurement

  • ERP

  • Reconciliation

  • Data platforms

  • Workflow management

  • AI-enabled exception management

Develop a scalable architecture connecting infrastructure telemetry to operational, commercial, and financial systems.

Establish dashboards and automated monitoring for control effectiveness, reconciliation exceptions, billing accuracy, supplier discrepancies, cost allocation, and financial leakage.

Create a prioritized automation backlog based on transaction volume, manual effort, financial risk, discrepancy rates, and business impact.

Track realized benefits from automation, including productivity improvements, reduced error rates, faster cycle times, and reduced operational cost.

Operating Metrics & Governance

Establish KPIs and KRIs measuring both the health of the underlying processes and progress toward automation

Lead regular cross-functional operating reviews to identify systemic issues, assign ownership, and drive remediation.

Use recurring exceptions and discrepancies as inputs into process redesign and automation priorities rather than treating them as isolated operational issues.

Provide management with transparency into operational risks, financial exposure, automation progress, and opportunities for further simplification.

Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership

Build and lead a high-performing Process & Controls organization as the company scales.

Act as the connective layer between AI Infrastructure, Engineering, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Sales Operations, Product, Data, and Internal Audit.

Establish clear accountability for processes that span multiple functions and systems.

Influence system architecture and operating-model decisions to ensure financial controls, data integrity, automation, and scalability are designed into processes from the beginning.

Create a culture of continuous improvement in which the organization moves from:

manual → standardized → controlled → automated → AI-enabled.

Balance operational rigor and financial control with the speed required in a rapidly evolving AI environment.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in process transformation, controllership, finance operations, business operations, internal controls, or related disciplines.

  • Significant leadership experience building or transforming complex, cross-functional processes.

  • Demonstrated experience establishing process foundations in environments with immature, fragmented, or rapidly evolving workflows.

  • Strong expertise in Order-to-Cash and Purchase-to-Pay processes.

  • Experience designing financial and operational control frameworks in technology, cloud infrastructure, SaaS, hyperscale infrastructure, or other consumption-based businesses.

  • Strong understanding of usage-based billing, metering, reconciliation, pricing, and consumption economics.

  • Track record of simplifying processes and reducing manual work through automation.

  • Experience partnering with Engineering, Data, Product, Finance, Accounting, and Procurement organizations.

  • Strong knowledge of ERP, billing, procurement, data, and financial systems.

  • Experience designing automated reconciliations and exception-management processes.

  • Familiarity with AI-enabled workflow automation, anomaly detection, and intelligent operations.

  • Familiarity with SOX, financial reporting controls, audit requirements, and accounting processes.

  • Ability to understand complex data flows and translate technical workflows into scalable business and financial processes.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience operating in a high-growth AI, cloud infrastructure, hyperscaler, or technology company.

  • Experience with consumption-based revenue and cost models.

  • Familiarity with cloud providers and AI infrastructure vendors.

  • Experience implementing or scaling usage metering, billing, FinOps, procurement, reconciliation, or workflow platforms.

  • Experience leading large-scale process clean-up, transformation, and automation programs.

What Success Looks Like

The Head of Process & Controls will transform the operating environment in three stages:

1. Build the foundation
Establish clear processes, ownership, controls, authoritative data, operating standards, and system accountability.

2. Clean up and stabilize
Eliminate fragmented workflows, recurring discrepancies, unnecessary manual activities, inconsistent data, and control gaps.

3. Automate and scale
Deploy automation and AI so routine activities, reconciliations, validations, and exception detection occur with minimal manual intervention.

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

Define clear end-to-end processes, ownership, controls, decision rights, system-of-records, data handoffs, approval points, exception paths, and escalation procedures.

Assess the current operating environment and identify:

 - Fragmented or undocumented processes

 - Manual workarounds

 - Spreadsheet-dependent workflows

 - Duplicate activities

 - Unclear process ownership

 - Control gaps

 - Inconsistent data definitions

 - Reconciliation issues

 - System integration gaps

 - Recurring operational and financial discrepancies

Lead the Standardization of existing processes before introducing automation, ensuring that inefficient or poorly controlled processes are not simply automated in their current state.

Develop standard operating procedures, process maps, RACI frameworks, control matrices, data definitions, and operational playbooks.

Establish consistent process and control standards across functions, regions, products, customers, and infrastructure providers.

Create a transformation roadmap that prioritizes foundational process improvements, risk remediation, automation opportunities, and scalable system capabilities.




AI AUTOMATION & MANUAL EFFORT REDUCTION

Lead the transition from manual and reactive operations toward AI-enabled, automated process execution and controls.

Identify high-volume, repetitive, reconciliation-intensive, and exception-driven activities that can be automated.

Partner with Engineering, Data, Finance Systems, and Product teams to implement AI-enabled workflows for areas such as:

 - Automated usage reconciliation

 - Token and compute anomaly detection

 - Customer billing validation

 - Vendor invoice validation

 - Contract-to-billing checks

 - Purchase-order and invoice matching

 - Revenue and cost leakage identification

 - Accrual estimation

 - Data-quality monitoring

 - Exception classification and routing

 - Root-cause analysis

 - Variance investigation

 - Duplicate or missing transaction detection

 - Automated control evidence collection

 - Operational reporting and management insights

Design processes around exception-based management, where systems and AI handle routine transactions and teams focus primarily on material exceptions, judgment, and remediation.

Establish measurable targets for reducing manual touchpoints, spreadsheet dependency, reconciliation effort, processing time, error rates, and discrepancies.

Ensure AI-enabled automation includes appropriate governance, human review, traceability, validation, and controls.


WORKFLOW & PROCESS GOVERNANCE

Standardize the end-to-end process framework for AI infrastructure operations, from infrastructure provisioning and consumption through usage measurement, customer billing, vendor settlement, accounting, and reporting.

Map and optimize workflows across compute, GPU, model inference, API and token consumption, capacity allocation, and related infrastructure services.

Establish clear process ownership, approval points, system interfaces, data handoffs, service-level expectations, exception management, and escalation procedures.

Partner with Engineering and Infrastructure teams to design operational processes that remain scalable as AI workloads, customers, infrastructure providers, and commercial models grow.

Ensure controls and financial requirements are embedded into infrastructure workflows by design rather than added downstream.


TOKEN & USAGE ACCURACY

Standardize framework governing the accuracy, completeness, and traceability of AI token and infrastructure usage data.

Ensure reliable measurement and reconciliation of metrics such as:

 - Input and output tokens

 - API consumption

 - Model inference usage

 - GPU or accelerator utilization

 - Compute hours

 - Storage and network consumption

 - Reserved and on-demand capacity

 - Customer-specific infrastructure consumption

Establish automated reconciliations between infrastructure telemetry, metering platforms, pricing systems, customer contracts, billing systems, supplier data, and the general ledger.

Develop preventive and detective controls to identify:

 - Missing usage

 - Duplicate usage

 - Incorrect token counts

 - Incorrect pricing

 - Unbilled consumption

 - Misallocated consumption

 - Customer/vendor usage mismatches

 - Unexpected consumption patterns

 - Data pipeline failures

Partner with Data and Engineering teams to establish authoritative data sources, common definitions, and end-to-end data lineage from infrastructure activity through financial reporting.

Drive continuous improvement in token accuracy, usage completeness, billing accuracy, and cost attribution.


ORDER-TO-CASH

Own and continuously improve the end-to-end Order-to-Cash process, including:

contract / order → provisioning → usage capture → rating and pricing → invoicing → accounts receivable → collections → revenue reporting.

Build a standardized and scalable O2C foundation that supports both committed and consumption-based business models.

Ensure customer contracts, pricing structures, committed capacity, minimum spend agreements, usage-based pricing, credits, and discounts are correctly translated into operational and billing systems.

Establish automated controls over usage-to-invoice reconciliation and billing completeness.

Reduce manual billing adjustments and recurring discrepancies through better upstream data quality, system integration, and automated validation.

Develop processes for billing adjustments, credits, disputes, contract amendments, and usage exceptions.

Partner with Revenue Accounting to ensure operational processes support accurate and timely revenue recognition.

Drive improvements in billing accuracy, invoice timeliness, collections, customer experience, and revenue leakage prevention.


PURCHASE-TO-PAY

Own and optimize the Purchase-to-Pay process for AI infrastructure and related services, including:

capacity planning → purchase commitment → purchase order → service consumption → invoice validation → accrual → payment → supplier reconciliation.

Build a standardized P2P foundation connecting procurement commitments, infrastructure usage, supplier contracts, invoices, and accounting.

Establish controls ensuring vendor invoices accurately reflect contracted pricing and actual infrastructure consumption.

Reduce manual invoice review and reconciliation through AI-enabled invoice validation and exception detection.

Partner with Infrastructure and Procurement teams on commitments for cloud services, GPUs, data centers, networking, model providers, and other infrastructure vendors.

Develop processes for committed-use agreements, prepaid capacity, minimum commitments, volume discounts, credits, and variable consumption charges.

Ensure appropriate accruals and cost allocations where supplier invoices lag infrastructure consumption.


FINANCIAL & OPERATIONAL CONTROLS

Design and maintain a scalable controls framework across infrastructure operations and financial processes.

Define preventive and detective controls covering:

 - Usage completeness and accuracy

 - Token accuracy

 - Pricing accuracy

 - Customer billing

 - Supplier invoicing

 - Revenue completeness

 - Infrastructure cost completeness

 - Contract compliance

 - Approval authorities

 - Reconciliations

 - Data integrity

 - Manual adjustments

Prioritize automated controls over manual controls wherever technically and operationally feasible.

Establish control owners, evidence requirements, review frequencies, exception thresholds, and remediation processes.

Create automated exception monitoring so discrepancies can be identified close to the point of occurrence rather than through downstream month-end reconciliation.

Partner with Accounting, Internal Audit, and external auditors to support financial reporting and audit requirements.

Where applicable, build processes and controls capable of supporting SOX-compliant operations.


PROCESS AUTOMATION, SYSTEMS & DATA ARCHITECTURE

Drive automation across infrastructure-to-finance workflows and systematically reduce reliance on spreadsheets, manual reconciliations, and human intervention.

Partner with Product, Engineering, Finance Systems, and Data teams to define requirements for:

 - Usage metering

 - Rating and pricing

 - Billing

 - Procurement

 - ERP

 - Reconciliation

 - Data platforms

 - Workflow management

 - AI-enabled exception management

Develop a scalable architecture connecting infrastructure telemetry to operational, commercial, and financial systems.

Establish dashboards and automated monitoring for control effectiveness, reconciliation exceptions, billing accuracy, supplier discrepancies, cost allocation, and financial leakage.

Create a prioritized automation backlog based on transaction volume, manual effort, financial risk, discrepancy rates, and business impact.

Track realized benefits from automation, including productivity improvements, reduced error rates, faster cycle times, and reduced operational cost.


OPERATING METRICS & GOVERNANCE

Establish KPIs and KRIs measuring both the health of the underlying processes and progress toward automation

Lead regular cross-functional operating reviews to identify systemic issues, assign ownership, and drive remediation.

Use recurring exceptions and discrepancies as inputs into process redesign and automation priorities rather than treating them as isolated operational issues.

Provide management with transparency into operational risks, financial exposure, automation progress, and opportunities for further simplification.




LEADERSHIP & CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PARTNERSHIP

Build and lead a high-performing Process & Controls organization as the company scales.

Act as the connective layer between AI Infrastructure, Engineering, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Sales Operations, Product, Data, and Internal Audit.

Establish clear accountability for processes that span multiple functions and systems.

Influence system architecture and operating-model decisions to ensure financial controls, data integrity, automation, and scalability are designed into processes from the beginning.

Create a culture of continuous improvement in which the organization moves from:

manual → standardized → controlled → automated → AI-enabled.

Balance operational rigor and financial control with the speed required in a rapidly evolving AI environment.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 10+ years of experience in process transformation, controllership, finance operations, business operations, internal controls, or related disciplines.

 - Significant leadership experience building or transforming complex, cross-functional processes.

 - Demonstrated experience establishing process foundations in environments with immature, fragmented, or rapidly evolving workflows.

 - Strong expertise in Order-to-Cash and Purchase-to-Pay processes.

 - Experience designing financial and operational control frameworks in technology, cloud infrastructure, SaaS, hyperscale infrastructure, or other consumption-based businesses.

 - Strong understanding of usage-based billing, metering, reconciliation, pricing, and consumption economics.

 - Track record of simplifying processes and reducing manual work through automation.

 - Experience partnering with Engineering, Data, Product, Finance, Accounting, and Procurement organizations.

 - Strong knowledge of ERP, billing, procurement, data, and financial systems.

 - Experience designing automated reconciliations and exception-management processes.

 - Familiarity with AI-enabled workflow automation, anomaly detection, and intelligent operations.

 - Familiarity with SOX, financial reporting controls, audit requirements, and accounting processes.

 - Ability to understand complex data flows and translate technical workflows into scalable business and financial processes.


PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

 - Experience operating in a high-growth AI, cloud infrastructure, hyperscaler, or technology company.

 - Experience with consumption-based revenue and cost models.

 - Familiarity with cloud providers and AI infrastructure vendors.

 - Experience implementing or scaling usage metering, billing, FinOps, procurement, reconciliation, or workflow platforms.

 - Experience leading large-scale process clean-up, transformation, and automation programs.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

The Head of Process & Controls will transform the operating environment in three stages:

1. Build the foundation
Establish clear processes, ownership, controls, authoritative data, operating standards, and system accountability.

2. Clean up and stabilize
Eliminate fragmented workflows, recurring discrepancies, unnecessary manual activities, inconsistent data, and control gaps.

3. Automate and scale
Deploy automation and AI so routine activities, reconciliations, validations, and exception detection occur with minimal manual intervention.



WHY FIREWORKS?

 - Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

 - Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

 - Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

 - Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

raw.title: Senior Privacy Specialist
raw.description:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

About the role

We're hiring a Senior Privacy Specialist to be our privacy presence in the UK and EU as Fireworks scales its European footprint. We've achieved ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001, and SOC 2 Type II, and we operate active UK GDPR, EU GDPR, and CCPA programs.

You'll be our senior privacy point of contact for the UK and EU - the person who fields supervisory authority correspondence and owns the operational processes that keep our UK GDPR, EU GDPR, and Data Protection Act 2018 obligations met. You'll report to our Privacy Lead and work as part of a small global privacy team, with real autonomy over the UK/EU side of the program.

This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role, and an advisory one. You'll be the privacy judgment in the room for the UK and EU: the person engineers, sales, and legal come to before they ship, sign, or answer.

Who this role is for

We're building a privacy function that punches well above its headcount. That shapes who succeeds here:

  • You've operated and built under ambiguity. You're used to being the one who owns it, and you've built structures where none existed rather than inheriting someone else's.

  • You build systems, not queues. You've used AI tooling, automation platforms, scripting, or workflow engines to take manual privacy work off the table - and you're excited to do more of that utilizing cutting-edge technology.

  • You take a project and finish it. You don't need prescriptive instructions or hand-holding - you spot what's broken, scope it, own it until completion, and socialize it within the organization.

  • You take extreme ownership. When something in your area goes wrong, you own it, fix it, and make sure it can't happen the same way twice - without waiting to be asked and without pointing fingers.

What you'll do

  • Act as our senior privacy point of contact for the UK and EU: first line for the ICO and EU supervisory authorities, handling regulator correspondence and inquiries with support from our Privacy Lead and Legal.

  • Be the standing privacy advisor for the region: guidance to product, engineering, GTM, and Legal on what UK/EU law permits, where the grey areas are, and what risk you're recommending we accept.

  • Own UK/EU data subject rights outcomes: statutory deadlines, scope and exemption decisions, edge cases, and the regional record.

  • Own cross-border transfer compliance: UK IDTA and Addendum, EU SCCs, adequacy analysis, and Transfer Impact Assessments for vendors, sub-processors, and intra-group flows.

  • Lead breach assessment and notification for UK/EU: triage, 72-hour notification decisions, regulator and data subject communications, and post-incident follow-through with Security and Legal.

  • Embed privacy-by-design into how we build: review new products, features, models, and vendors for privacy risk, and give engineering and product teams guidance they can act on.

  • Partner with our AI governance work on privacy in model training, fine-tuning, and inference - data minimization, purpose limitation, customer data handling, and emerging EU AI Act obligations.

  • Keep the UK/EU privacy notice and policy library accurate, practical, and aligned to what we actually do and our regulatory obligations.

  • Take on additional privacy projects as the program evolves; we're a growing team with dynamic priorities.

How the role will grow

As the program matures and our European footprint expands, you'll have the opportunity to:

  • Regional ownership - take on privacy for additional jurisdictions as we enter new markets, and shape our approach to emerging regimes.

  • Advisory reach - become the privacy voice in the highest-stakes decisions: new markets, new product categories, regulator engagement, and AI Act readiness.

  • Program ownership - take a hand in setting program direction, roadmap, and strategy.

What we're looking for

  • 5-7 years of experience in privacy or data protection, with meaningful time in a tech, SaaS, or cloud company.

  • Deep, hands-on working knowledge of UK GDPR, EU GDPR, and the Data Protection Act 2018 - you've been a key player in a program complying with these regimes, not just worked on a small portion of one.

  • Experience as the sole or primary privacy owner for a region, product, or company; you're comfortable without a large team around you.

  • Track record running DPIAs and DSARs hands-on, and advising product and engineering teams on privacy-by-design.

  • Direct experience with international transfer mechanisms (UK IDTA, SCCs, adequacy, TIAs) and the judgment to apply them to real vendor and architecture decisions.

  • Some exposure to a supervisory authority - whether as a DPO, deputy, or otherwise.

  • Excellent communication; you work confidently across engineering, legal, sales, and executive audiences, and you can turn regulatory requirements into clear guidance.

  • Comfort with low-code automation and LLM-based tooling - enough to specify, evaluate, and get hands-on with the systems that run your program.

  • Based in the EU/UK with the right to work in those geographies.

Nice to have

  • Privacy certifications (CIPP/E, CIPM, CIPT, FIP).

  • Experience with privacy tooling (OneTrust, TrustArc, Transcend, DataGrail, Securiti, or similar) - especially if you've pushed one past its out-of-the-box limits.

  • Exposure to ISO 42001, AI/ML data governance, model training data considerations, or the EU AI Act.

  • Experience standing up a privacy function in-region at a growth-stage company.

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

About the role

We're looking for a Privacy Program Engineer to own the technical core of our privacy program. We've achieved ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001, and SOC 2 Type II, and we run active GDPR and CCPA/CPRA programs - now we need someone to run the machinery that keeps all of it working, and to make that machinery largely run itself.

This is a privacy role with real technical depth - you'll write scripts, queries, and automation. From day one you'll own real workstreams: data subject requests, the data inventory and ROPA, hands-on privacy reviews for new vendors and features.. You'll report to our Privacy Lead and be a key owner of large portions of our privacy program, as well as the key technical expert on the privacy team.

This is not a ticket queue with a title. We're a small team at a company that builds AI infrastructure, and we intend to leverage it - you'll own the direction and design of the technical systems, automations, and tools that help us meet our privacy obligations at Fireworks.

Who this role is for

  • You build systems, not queues. You've used AI tooling, automation, scripting, or workflow platforms to eliminate manual privacy work.

  • You're technical enough to be dangerous. You read code to understand what a service actually does with data. You can query a database without asking for help. You've automated something real with code, a workflow engine, or an LLM-based agent and you know how to build scalable tools running against production systems and data.

  • You take a project and run with it. Given a rough problem and a deadline, you come back with it done. You’re not afraid to make tactical decisions and judgement calls.

  • You take extreme ownership. You're comfortable owning something outright and figuring it out - your workstreams are yours. You surface problems early, fix them, and make sure they don't recur.

raw.title: Member of Technical Staff, Growth
raw.description:
About Us:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.

The Role

We're building a new Product-Led Growth (PLG) team, and we're looking for a creative, high-agency product engineer to be one of its first engineers.

You'll build Fireworks' growth platform: the systems and experiences that take a developer from first visit, to first successful API call, to a long-term, expanding customer.

There's an early roadmap ready, but the market moves quickly, and you'll be expected to help diagnose customer problems, ideate on solutions, and experiment to find what works.

The surface area includes signup, onboarding, docs, the API and playground, model choice, errors, pricing, billing, and lifecycle messaging, across inference, training, and the rest of the platform. Some of what's on the table:

  • Acquisition to product. Connect how developers discover Fireworks to what they do once they arrive, so every first experience feels built for them.

  • Activation and onboarding. Cut time to first working request. Useful errors, docs that match the product, the right default model, and a reason to come back.

  • Experimentation. Build the tools and habits that let the whole company test ideas fast and learn from them.

  • Trust at scale. Make getting started effortless while keeping the platform safe and reliable for everyone.

  • Monetization and expansion. Help developers grow with Fireworks, from first project to production scale.

What You'll Do

  • Own developer outcomes end to end: find the problem, shape the solution, prototype, ship to production, instrument, and learn from the results.

  • Build the growth foundations the team doesn't have yet: event tracking, funnels, an experimentation framework, and lifecycle messaging.

  • Design and run experiments with rigor (clear hypotheses, the right metrics, honest readouts), and know when to ship an obvious win without a test.

  • Talk to developers directly. Watch them build, see where the first call fails, and bring that back as working code.

  • Craft polished, fast, accessible experiences on our marketing site and in the product.

  • Dig into funnel and cohort data to find the next bet, and communicate what you find clearly.

  • Work closely with product, design, marketing, data, and sales, so self-serve growth works alongside our sales-led motion.

  • Use AI coding tools to move quickly, while owning the quality of everything you ship.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years building and shipping user-facing products, including real time on product or growth surfaces as a senior, staff, or founding engineer.

  • A track record of moving business metrics. You can point to specific numbers you changed and how.

  • Strong full-stack skills: TypeScript/React on the front end, plus backend services (Go a plus), APIs, data models, and SQL.

  • A product engineer mindset. You define the problem and the solution, not just the implementation.

  • A designer's eye. You care about interaction details, copy, and how a flow feels, and you can make a technical product feel simple.

  • Hands-on experience with A/B testing, funnel analysis, and product analytics.

  • Genuine high agency. You've started things nobody asked you to, pushed them through without a mandate, and owned the result when it didn't work.

  • A bias toward action. You ship in days, not quarters, and you'd rather pick the right problem than wait to be assigned one.

  • Comfort in ambiguity, and the ability to lead without authority across product, design, marketing, and data.

  • Clear written and verbal communication with engineers and non-engineers.

  • A Bachelor's or Master's degree in CS, EE, or equivalent experience.

Nice to Have

  • Growth, activation, or monetization experience at a developer-tools, API, or infra company.

  • Experience building developer-facing products (APIs, SDKs, dev tools, consoles).

  • Experience with consumption or usage-based pricing and billing.

  • Experience building PLG or self-serve inside a company that also sells top-down.

  • Experience with trust & safety or identity systems.

  • You've built with LLM APIs and have opinions on what great developer onboarding for AI looks like.

  • A portfolio, side projects, or launches that show your taste and range. Non-traditional paths welcome. We care about what you've shipped and the judgment behind it.

How We'll Evaluate

We'll look closely at work you personally identified, built, and shipped, and what you learned after launch. Come ready to walk us through a time you saw a problem no one owned, decided to fix it, and drove it to a measurable outcome. Expect a practical product and engineering exercise, not pure algorithm puzzles.

 

Fireworks AI is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification.

Why Fireworks?

  • Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving.

  • Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally.

  • Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results.

  • Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation.

Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators.
